Leave granted.
Tag with SLP [Crl.] Nos.13836-13842/2024.
The appellant was convicted by the Special
Court for the offences punishable under Sections
302, 364, 201, 120-B read with Section 34 of the
Indian  Penal  Code,  1860  (for  short  ‘IPC’),
Sections  3(1)(ii),  3(2)  and  3(4)  of  the
Maharashtra Control of Organized Crime Act, 1999
(for short, ‘MCOC Act’). He was sentenced to
undergo rigorous imprisonment for life. The High
Court, in appeal upheld the conviction  qua the
offences punishable under Sections 302, 364 and
201 read with Section 34 of the IPC, however, it
set  aside  the  conviction  for  the  offences
punishable under the MCOC Act, 1999 and upheld the
sentence awarded to the appellant. 

--- Page 384 ---
3
We have heard the learned counsel appearing
for the parties.
Taking  into  consideration  the  facts  and
circumstances of the present appeal, coupled with
the fact that the appellant has already undergone
a period of 12 years under incarceration without
remission and 18 years including the period of
remission, we are inclined to suspend the sentence
imposed on the appellant, during the pendency of
the present appeal.
Accordingly, the sentence of the appellant
stands suspended and he is granted bail, during
the pendency of the present appeal, subject to the
terms and conditions to the satisfaction of the
concerned Trial Court.
Ordered accordingly.

which in the writ petition filed by the borrower, it has been

--- Page 398 ---
contd..
- 2 -
held that right of redemption is available to the borrower
despite issuance of sale certificate and execution of the sale
deed. The High Court noted that the borrower has deposited a sum
of Rs. 14,00,000/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs only) with the banks to
show his bona fides on 06.06.2025. Accordingly, the writ petition
was allowed.
3. Admittedly, the borrower is in possession of the property in
question. During the pendency of this Special Leave Petition,
the parties arrived at some kind of a settlement. It has been
stated before us that the petitioner would be satisfied if a sum
of Rs. 20,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs only) is paid to him.
4. The petitioner had deposited a sum of Rs. 13.65 Lakhs as sale
consideration with the bank. The said amount shall be returned
to the petitioner by the bank.
5. In addition, the respondent-borrower shall refund a sum of Rs.
6.35 Lakhs to the petitioner within a period of four months
from today. 
6. The respondent-borrower had deposited a sum of Rs. 14,00,000/-
(Rupees Fourteen Lakhs only) with the banks on 06.06.2025.
Therefore, the bank shall refund the aforesaid amount along
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum to the respondent-
borrower.
7. Accordingly, the Special Leave Petition stands disposed of.

Petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (C)  No(s).14082/2026
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 23-05-2025
in WRIT-A No. 7320/2025 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Allahabad]
AKANKSHA DEVI                                      Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
STATE OF UP & ORS.                                 Respondent(s)
IA No. 107394/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
IA No. 107406/2026 - PERMISSION TO FILE ADDITIONAL 
DOCUMENTS/FACTS/ANNEXURES
IA No. 252291/2026 - PERMISSION TO FILE ADDITIONAL 
DOCUMENTS/FACTS/ANNEXURES
 
Date : 15-09-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARAVIND KUMAR
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIPUL M. PANCHOLI
For Petitioner(s) :Ms. Alpana Sharma, AOR
                   Mr. N. K. Mody, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Alok Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Sandeep Kumar Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Vinay Namdeo Bambole, Adv.
                   Ms. Ishita M. Puranik, Adv.

                   Ms. Sakshi Rewaria, Adv.
                   Mr. Sameer Malik, Adv.
                   
                   
For Respondent(s) :Ms. Ruchira Goel, AOR
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The short issue which arises for consideration in the present petition
relates to recruitment of the petitioner to the post of constable civil police under
U.P. Police Constable Civil Direct Recruitment, 2023. Petitioner was issued a call
1

--- Page 413 ---
letter by the competent authority for document verification (DV) and physical
standard test (PST) requiring her to appear at Reserves Police Line, Kanpur
Dehat on 28.12.2024 at 09:00 am and successfully cleared the said tests and
her name was included in the qualified list of candidates for the next phase of
selection as evident from annexure-P4. Hence, petitioner was issued call letter
for medical examination to appear before the Medical Board constituted by the
competent authority. The examination was scheduled to be held on 22.04.2025
as intimated to the petitioner vide call letter dated 15.04.2025 annexure-P5.
Accordingly the petitioner appeared before the medical board on 22.04.2025
and she is said to have been orally informed by the examining authority that
she was unfit due to alleged defect in the eyes (squint eye). After her rejection
in the medical examination conducted on 22.04.2025 a re-examination was
conducted by the Division Medical Board, on 25.04.2025 as per Rule 15(6)(d)
which again declared her medically unfit on account of squint. However, no
rejection  order or endorsement  was  furnished  to the  petitioner.  Hence,
petitioner is said to have independently approached two qualified medical
institutions  including  Dr.  Parvej  Khan,  Professor  and  Dean  of  the  Eye
Department, G.S.V.M Medical College and Associated Hospital, Kanpur and Dr.
Rizwan Ahmad M.S. Consultant Eye Surgeon, UHM District Hospital, Kanpur
Nagar, who found her colour perception/variation were normal including vision
and thereby casting a serious doubt on the correctness and fairness of the initial
medical assessment made by the medical board constituted by the respondent-
authority. Based on these two reports, petitioner submitted a representation on
16.05.2025 seeking for a fresh medical examination before an independent
institution or competent authority including the Chief Medical Officer, Lucknow.
Same having been rejected, she  approached the jurisdictional High Court for a
2

--- Page 414 ---
direction to re-conduct the medical examination which came to be dismissed by
the impugned order on the ground of selection process having been concluded.
Hence, this petition.
2. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the parties, we have
noticed this Court in similar circumstances in SLP (C) No.17704/2025 titled as
“Sonam Devi vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Ors.” had observed as under:
Since a categorical stand was taken before us that the
appellant is medically fit and has no eye-related issue(s)
which could disqualify her from serving as a Constable, vide
our order dated 24.07.2025, we directed the King George’s
Medical  University,  a  Government  Medical  College  &
Hospital  in  Lucknow  to  constitute  a  Medical  Board,
comprising 2-3 eye-experts and render their opinion with
respect to the medical fitness of the appellant.
in view of the same and taking note of the fact that petitioner is similarly
placed. We are of the view an independent averment is to be made namely to
ascertain the medical fitness of the petitioner. Hence, we hereby direct the
petitioner to appear before King George’s Medical University, Government
Medical College and Hospital in Lucknow and the Director of the University shall
constitute a medical board comprising of 3 eye experts and after examination of
petitioner they shall render their opinion with respect to the medical fitness of
the appellant and specifically with reference to the squint. The said report shall
be submitted expeditiously and preferably within four weeks from today. Copy
of this Order be forwarded to the Dean or Director of King George’s Medical
University forthwith by the Registry.
3. List on 26.10.2026.
(DEEPANSHU)                                     (AVGV RAMU)
SENIOR PERSONAL ASSISTANT                     COURT MASTER (NSH)

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
INHERENT JURISDICTION 
REVIEW PETITION (C) ……….D. No.  25168 OF 2024
IN
CIVIL APPEAL Nos. 6521, 6525, 6526, 6527, 6528, 6529 and 6530  OF 2023
M/S DHARAMPAL PREMCHAND LTD.            … PETITIONER
Versus
COMMISSIONER, CENTRAL GOODS AND SERVICES TAX           … RESPONDENT
      
O  R  D  E  R
1. The application for listing the Review Petitions in open Court is rejected.
2. The Review Petitions are defective for the reasons stated in the Office
Report. The defects were notified to counsel for the petitioner by way of Registry’s
letter dated 27.06.2024 and 29.07.2024 but he has not cured the same so far.
3. However,  instead  of  rejecting  these  Review  Petitions  for  non-
prosecution, we have perused the same and the Judgment dated 20.10.2023 sought
to be reviewed. In our opinion, no case for review of the Judgment dated 20.10.2023
is made out.
4. We, however, notice an inadvertent textual inconsistency in paragraph
110 and paragraph 143(b) of the Judgment, wherein, despite recording the finding
that the orders of the adjudicating authority deserve to be upheld, the judgment
erroneously and inadvertently records that the orders of the Tribunal “ would not be

--- Page 446 ---
2
sustainable” and that the appeals “deserve to be allowed”. The said paragraph shall,
accordingly, stand substituted in the following terms:
“110. In the light of the findings recorded herein above, we are of the
considered view that the impugned orders of the tribunal do not call
for interference and the order of the adjudicating authority deserve to
be upheld, consequently these appeals deserve to be dismissed,
except the Civil Appeal arising out of Diary No. 3487 of 2020 which is
directed against the order dated 06.11.2019 passed by the CESTAT in
Excise Appeal No. 70242 of 2018, which stands on a different footing
and hence the said appeal is taken up for consideration and disposed
of by the following order”.
5. The aforesaid substitution is in conformity with the reasoning and the
operative portion of the Judgment dated 20.10.2023. Other than this typographical
correction, we do not find any other ground to entertain these Review Petitions.
6. With this clarification, the Review Petitions are disposed of. Pending
application(s), if any, shall stand closed.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Criminal Appeal  No.1362/2022
MAQSOOD AHMAD BHAT                                 Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF JAMMU AND KASHMIR                     Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and
having gone through the materials on record, we are of the view that no
error, not to speak of any error of law, could be said to have been
committed by the High Court in passing the impugned Judgment and Order.
2. However, we take notice of the fact that the incident in question is
of the year 2005.
3. The appellant - convict was put to trial for the offence of murder,
punishable under Section 302 of the Ranbir Penal Code read with Sections
7 and 27 of the Arms Act respectively.
4. By Judgment and Order dated 4th April, 2014, the appellant was held
guilty  of  the  alleged  crime  and  was  sentenced  to  undergo  life
imprisonment.
5. He went in appeal before the High Court. The appeal also came to be
dismissed.
6. It appears that in all, approximately the appellant was in jail for
18 years before this Court released him on bail. 
7. In such circumstances, it shall be open for the appellant to prefer
an appropriate representation addressed to the competent authority of the
Union  Territory  and  pray  for  remission  of  sentence.  If  any  such
representation is preferred by the appellant, the Competent Authority

--- Page 506 ---
2
shall look into the same expeditiously and take an appropriate decision
on the same, keeping in mind the remission policy of the UT prevailing on
the date of the commission of the alleged crime or any other remission
policy that may be beneficial to the appellant – convict. We also take
notice of the fact that the appellant came to be released by this Court
on bail vide Order dated 1st March, 2024. For the purpose of considering
the plea of remission, the appellant’s overall conduct after 1st March,
2024 may also be taken into consideration by the Competent Authority.
8. The decision shall be taken within a period of eight weeks from the
date of receipt of the representation, and the outcome of the same shall
be informed to the appellant - convict in writing.
9. We grant four weeks’ time to the appellant – convict to prefer an
appropriate representation.
10. Till the representation is decided by the UT, the appellant shall
continue to remain on bail.
11. With the aforesaid, this appeal stands disposed of.
12. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
…………………………………………J     
(J.B. PARDIWALA)
…………………………………………J     
(K. VINOD CHANDRAN)
NEW DELHI;
15TH SEPTEMBER, 2026.

1. This transfer petition has been filed by the

titled  “Nitesh  Balyan  vs.  Sachina”  from  the  Family

been effected on the respondent through the concerned
trial  Court.  No  one  has  entered  appearance  despite
service.
3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and perused
the material placed on record.
4. We have considered the facts of the case and grounds
on  which  transfer  has  been  sought.   On  such
consideration, we are satisfied with the grounds urged
by the petitioner and accept the same. Therefore, case
bearing HMA No.2675 of 2025 titled  “Nitesh  Balyan  vs.
Sachina”  pending before the Family Court, Dwarka, Delhi
1

--- Page 509 ---
is  ordered  to  be  transferred  to  the  Family  Court,
District Jhajjar, Haryana.
5. Records  of  the  case  should  immediately  be
transferred to the transferee court.

settlement through Mediation. The transferee court would
obtain the desire and wishes of the parties and proceed
accordingly in this regard.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following

1. The matrimonial dispute between the Petitioner-Husband and
Respondent No.2-Wife was amicably resolved through a settlement, on
the basis of which IA No.164606/2025 was filed, seeking invocation
of the powers of this Court under Article 142 of the Constitution.
Accepting that prayer, the order dated 19.08.2025 was passed by a
two-judge bench of this Court, in terms whereof, all the cases
between the parties were closed and a decree of divorce by mutual
1

--- Page 527 ---
consent was granted, subject to the Petitioner-Husband paying a
lump-sum alimony of Rs.40 lakhs by the to the Respondent No.2-Wife
in four installments of Rs.10 lakhs each beginning from 10.09.2026.
2. In deference thereto, the Petitioner-Husband has deposited a
sum of Rs.40 lakhs with the Registry of this Court. It was,
however, reported by the Registry that Respondent No.2-Wife had not
come forward to receive the amount. This Court, therefore,  vide
order dated 17.12.2025, directed Respondent No.2-Wife to furnish
her bank account details to the Registry so that the entire amount
could be transferred to that account. Unfortunately, no contact
could be established with her thereafter, as was reported by her
Advocate-on-Record on 17.07.2026.
3. Today, Respondent No.2-Wife, Ms. Kalpana Kumari is present as
party-in-person in Court. She has shown her Aadhaar Card to enable
us to verify her identity. The fact that she contacted the learned
counsel for the Petitioner-Husband for the release of the amount
also fortifies the submission that Respondent No.2-Wife has now
voluntarily come forward to receive the amount. She states that the
details of her bank account shall be furnished to the Registry
during the course of the day. On doing so, we direct the Registry
to transfer the entire amount of Rs.40 lakhs along with the
interest accrued thereon, to the account of Respondent No.2-Wife as
early as possible, but not later than one week.
4. In view of the fact that the directions contained in our order
dated 19.08.2025 regarding payment of permanent alimony have been
complied with by the Petitioner-Husband, the directions contained
in the said order, especially in paragraph Nos.12 and 13, are made
2

--- Page 528 ---
absolute. The Family Court at Patna is, accordingly, directed to
draw up a decree of divorce.

application(s), if any.

                             O R D E R
1. State of Uttar Pradesh has instituted this special leave petition challenging
the order of the High Court which has, on facts and circumstances, granted the
claim of the respondents for refund of stamp duty in a sum of Rs.4 lakh +
overruling the objection that such claim was time-barred. 
2. This special leave petition is time-barred. While the State is aggrieved
because a time-barred claim was allowed, the least expected of it was to
approach this Court within the prescribed period of limitation.  
3. Since the State itself has approached this Court beyond the period of
1

--- Page 545 ---
limitation, it cannot expect a favourable consideration of its application for
condonation of delay. 
4. The special leave petition is dismissed only on this ground, without
examining the State’s claim on merits. Question of law, if any, is kept open.

justified.

the case, consequently while keeping the question of
law open, we dismiss the Special Leave Petition.

to move the Industrial Court for payment of arrears,
salary, etc. in installments. We express no opinion
in this regard.
